input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: the wrapper now clears and reuses one statistics dict for every call instead of giving each call its own, so concurrent or nested calls of the same decorated function write into the same dict
- failure path: two threads (or two concurrent awaits of the async wrapper) call the same decorated function; the second call's stats.clear() wipes the first call's start_time and attempt_number, and both read a merged, wrong statistics view afterwards

Reviewer finding
- description: All concurrent or nested invocations of the same wrapped function now share and clear a single statistics dict. Previously each call got its own copy's statistics.
- rationale: Trigger: two threads (or recursive calls) invoke the same decorated function at once. Each call runs stats.clear() and then writes into the same dict. One call resets the other's attempt_number and start_time mid-run, so the statistics are corrupted. If the retry logic reads the stats (for example attempt_number for stop conditions), retry behavior can be wrong as well.
critique: The finding names the same mechanism as the label. A single statistics dict is shared and cleared across concurrent or nested calls, so one call's clear() wipes another's start_time and attempt_number. That is exactly the labeled root cause and failure path.
